details: Recorded as part of CRS, without evidence that the TCR recognized PRAME in hepatocytes.
No marrow MAGE-A4 or enrichment of engineered T cells was detected; conditioning and systemic inflammation were considered contributors.
Occurred after grade 3 neurotoxicity; no demonstrated MAGE-A4-specific brain injury mechanism was reported.

details: Mechanistic work identified titin as the likely unintended target; MAGE antigens were not detected in patient heart samples.

Required intensive supportive care; symptoms resolved. The subsequent death of this patient was attributed to disease progression.

details: Authors favored intensified lymphodepletion; patient marrow antigen testing was limited. Fatality was 98 days after the second infusion.

details: Cytokine-mediated capillary leak was favored, but normal-peptide recognition remained a possibility. Below grade 4 does not mean clinically irrelevant.

details: Two deaths among three neurological cases in nine treated patients; the third recovered. Attribution of normal brain antigen to MAGE-A12 is proposed rather than exclusive.
